scope: Original 7,283 PINNS windows at four previously examined sites. Pose inference is omitted. Map generation, cropping and window eligibility do not require pose outputs. V2 does not archive per-window map tensors, so cross-version decoder/OpenCV bitwise identity is unverified. The later 1,482-window M0/M1 held-out-site study does not use this map.

source.dataset: Official PINNS release, labels, scene calibrations and BEV video; no road vector annotations used

sources_by_channel.bev_contour: Generic Canny image contour from a seven-frame median; no manually labeled curb/sidewalk mask
sources_by_channel.parked_rectangle: Synthetic axis-aligned 4.2 x 1.8 m rectangle at rounded fixed non-pedestrian centers; no instances
sources_by_channel.pedestrian_hull: Closed convex hull of training pedestrian positions; no annotated portal or walkable boundary
sources_by_channel.tangent_valid: Geometric flag on generic image contours

definition: Per-channel counts are windows with one or more active lines, and instances of active lines. Local extraction uses a 20 m nearest-original-vertex radius, 16 lines maximum, 10 points per line. PINNS always sets m_map=1. A usable hull vertex match compares original float32 global vertices, before resampling; identical coordinates can have multiple contributing rows. Track matches require the same clip and person ID. Split-trigger spans run from the first to the last eligible 10 Hz anchor, expressed as raw zero-based BEV frames (3*t under the frozen convention). Timing exposure does not establish that a moving object survives the median or affects a prediction.
